game: Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets@Virginia Tech Hokies

guide_enrichment.narrative:
What stands out to us is the gap between Virginia Tech’s surface-level defensive results and the underlying matchup. We see Georgia Tech creating scoring opportunities efficiently and holding an advantage through the air, while our numbers are less convinced by Virginia Tech’s ability to prevent those opportunities. That differs from a résumé that shows Virginia Tech allowing 274.4 yards and 19.8 points per game through five games.

We also see clear reasons not to push that disagreement too far. Virginia Tech recorded 51 tackles for loss and 18 sacks through five games, giving its defense a way to disrupt drives before Georgia Tech can exploit the favorable areas our model identifies. On the other side, Ethan Grunkemeyer completed 74.0 percent of his passes through five games, and Virginia Tech’s rushing attack has a favorable efficiency matchup against Georgia Tech’s run defense. For us, those counterweights leave the current price short of what we would need to move beyond a pass.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Georgia Tech’s passing offense against Virginia Tech’s pressure. The Yellow Jackets’ passing efficiency is central to our model’s disagreement with the market, but Virginia Tech’s pass rush can change that equation: Aycen Stevens produced 5.5 sacks through five games and recorded at least one solo sack in each. If Georgia Tech keeps its passing game on schedule, our view becomes easier to justify; if Virginia Tech consistently creates negative plays, the apparent advantage can disappear quickly.
